cc001.committed_to: Harvard University (confirmed committed, currently enrolled per author's own statement)
cc001.note: Male, White, FGLI, domestic/urban Massachusetts public school (non-competitive). SAT 1540 (780 RW/760 M); 8 APs + 3 dual-enrollment courses (AP CS Principles 4, Lang 5, Seminar 5, Physics 4). Legislative intern at MA State House (research helped convince a rep to co-sponsor migrant-rights legislation); founding member of Model UN; co-founder of Debate Club; founder/editor of school newspaper; student journalist; summer-program counselor for high-needs students; founder of chess club; math club president; 4-year SkillsUSA competitor. Applied Harvard/Williams/Brandeis/UMass Amherst; accepted Harvard, Williams, UMass Amherst; waitlisted Brandeis. Author's own retrospective: credits improved outcome to refocusing ECs specifically toward government/economics interest area between an initial (weaker) profile and the final application. cc005.title: Actual Results with Net Cost—Suburban NY, WF, CS, 1550+, 4.0 UW
cc005.gpa: 4.0 UW / 4.52 W (parent's estimate; school uses a 100-point scale)
cc005.class_rank: 2 of 198 (only knew 'top decile' at the time of applying)
cc005.honors_awards: National Merit Finalist; two summer research programs (one described as well-known); FRC robotics team 'Programming Captain'
cc005.committed_to: MIT (confirmed committed), Early Action, ~$20k net cost to the family
cc005.note: PARENT-AUTHORED post (mother posting on her daughter's behalf) — a useful distinct-perspective source versus this archive's mostly student-authored entries. SAT 1590 (800 M / 790 V). Seven APs, all scored 5 (CS A, Bio, World History, Calc BC, Physics 1, US History, Lang & Comp), plus Multivariable Calculus and Linear Algebra taken online with A's. Intended CS major. Good-but-not-exceptional ECs per the parent's own characterization: FRC robotics, music, volunteer/service including a self-described 'passion project,' some awards, two summer research programs; explicitly no sports. Also accepted, with net cost of attendance for each: Stony Brook (in-state, WISE honors program, <$25k est.), Binghamton (in-state EA, First Year Research Immersion + $3,500 stipend, ~$28k), RPI (EA, -$42k merit, $35k), UMass Amherst (OOS EA honors, -$16k, $38k), Drexel (EA, -$36k combined merit+need, $39k), Northeastern (EA honors + Global Experience stipend, ~$25.5-28k merit, COA uncertain/as high as $56k due to no need-based offer despite follow-up calls), UMD (OOS EA, Advanced Cybersecurity Experience Honors College, -$12k, $43k), Pitt (rolling OOS, Honors + GAP, -$15k, $43k), WPI (EA, -$27.5k, $49k). UChicago EA: withdrew application after MIT acceptance. BU: waitlisted (declined the spot). Did not end up applying to several originally-planned RD reaches (Harvard, Princeton, Yale, CMU, Brown, Harvey Mudd, Stanford) once the EA admit to first choice (MIT) settled the process. Includes extensive parent-perspective process advice (apply to at least one early-rolling school; demonstrated interest matters where stated; run net price calculators rather than assuming no aid; application burnout is real). Source: College Confidential, Chance Me / Match Me subforum, standalone post.
